newsitem.title: CHINA: China October retail inflation 4.7 pct - TV.
newsitem.headline: China October retail inflation 4.7 pct - TV.

text.p: China's retail price inflation was 4.7 percent in October, state television said on Monday.
State television, quoting figures from the State Statistical Bureau, said the data showed continued price stability.
It also quoted the State Planning Commission as calling for continued efforts to maintain stable retail price conditions and to implement national grain policy to protect the interests of farmers.

Chinese leaders have called on local officials to ensure that purchases of grain from farmers be made at state-set prices and that government funds earmarked for grain purchases be used for their stated purpose.
China has brought inflation down well below the target level of 10 percent for all of 1996.
The central bank chief has said inflation for the full year should be below 6.6 percent. That would compare with 14.8 percent last year.
Retail price inflation from January to October was 6.4 percent, the official Xinhua news agency said.

The southern province of Hainan had the lowest inflation rate of any province during the period at 2.4 percent while the northwestern region of Xinjiang showed the highest at 9.3 percent, Xinhua said.
